arxiv-2008-08826.title: Simultaneous Detection and Tracking with Motion Modelling for Multiple Object Tracking
arxiv-2008-08826.creator: ShiJie Sun, Naveed Akhtar, XiangYu Song, HuanSheng Song, Ajmal Mian, Mubarak Shah
arxiv-2008-08826.description: Abstract Deep learning based Multiple Object Tracking (MOT) currently relies on off-the-shelf detectors for tracking-by-detection. This results in deep models that are detector biased and evaluations that are detector influenced. To resolve this issue, we introduce Deep Motion Modeling Network (DMM-Net) that can estimate multiple objects’ motion parameters to perform joint detection and association in an end-to-end manner.

arxiv-2307-06033.title: AI-Generated Imagery: A New Era for the ‘Readymade’
arxiv-2307-06033.creator: Amy Smith, Michael Cook
arxiv-2307-06033.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Amy Smith, Michael Cook. While the term ‘art’ defies any concrete definition, this paper aims to examine how digital images produced by generative AI systems, such as Midjourney, have come to be so regularly referred to as such. The discourse around the classification of AI-generated imagery as art is currently somewhat homogeneous, lacking the more nuanced aspects that would apply to more traditional modes of artistic media production.

arxiv-2308-11023.title: Statistical Prediction of [CII] Observations by Constructing Probability Density Functions using SOFIA, Herschel, and Spitzer Observations
arxiv-2308-11023.creator: Young Min Seo 1, Karen Willacy 1, Umaa Rebbapragada 1
arxiv-2308-11023.description: Abstract We present a statistical algorithm for predicting the [CII] emission from Herschel and Spitzer continuum images using probability density functions between the [CII] emission and continuum emission. The [CII] emission at 158 μ \mu m is a critical tracer in studying the life cycle of interstellar medium and galaxy evolution.

arxiv-2311-10985.title: Lyman- α \alpha at Cosmic Noon I: Ly α \alpha Spectral Type Selection of z ∼ 2 − 3 z\sim 2-3 Lyman Break Galaxies with Broadband Imaging DOI: 10.1017/pasa.2023.48
arxiv-2311-10985.creator: Garry Foran, Jeff Cooke, Naveen Reddy, Charles Steidel, Alice Shapley
arxiv-2311-10985.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Garry Foran, Jeff Cooke, Naveen Reddy, Charles Steidel, Alice Shapley. High-redshift Lyman break galaxies (LBGs) are efficiently selected in deep images using as few as three broadband filters, and have been shown to have multiple intrinsic and small- to large-scale environmental properties related to Lyman- α \alpha . In this paper we demonstrate a statistical relationship between net Lyman- α \alpha equivalent width (net Ly α \alpha EW) and the optical broadband photometric properties of LBGs at z ∼ 2 z\sim 2 .

arxiv-2408-14728.title: TART: Boosting Clean Accuracy Through Tangent Direction Guided Adversarial Training
arxiv-2408-14728.creator: Bongsoo Yi, Rongjie Lai, Yao Li
arxiv-2408-14728.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Bongsoo Yi, Rongjie Lai, Yao Li. Adversarial training has been shown to be successful in enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks against adversarial attacks. However, this robustness is accompanied by a significant decline in accuracy on clean data. In this paper, we propose a novel method, called Tangent Direction Guided Adversarial Training (TART), that leverages the tangent space of the data manifold to ameliorate the existing adversarial defense algorithms.

arxiv-2507-21638.title: Assistax: A Hardware-Accelerated Reinforcement Learning Benchmark for Assistive Robotics
arxiv-2507-21638.creator: Leonard Hinckeldey, Elliot Fosong, Elle Miller, Rimvydas Rubavicius, Trevor McInroe, Patricia Wollstadt, Christiane B. Wiebel-Herboth, Subramanian Ramamoorthy, Stefano V. Albrecht
arxiv-2507-21638.description: Abstract The development of reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms has been largely driven by ambitious challenge tasks and benchmarks. Games have dominated RL benchmarks because they present relevant challenges, are inexpensive to run and easy to understand. While games such as Go and Atari have led to many breakthroughs, they often do not directly translate to real-world embodied applications.

arxiv-2509-24745.title: ProxyAttn: Guided Sparse Attention via Representative Heads
arxiv-2509-24745.creator: Yixuan Wang, Huang He, Siqi Bao, Haifeng Wang, Qingfu Zhu, Wanxiang Che
arxiv-2509-24745.description: Abstract The quadratic complexity of attention mechanisms limits the efficiency of Large Language Models (LLMs) on long-text tasks. Recently, methods that dynamically estimate block importance have enabled efficient block sparse attention, leading to significant acceleration in long-text pre-filling of LLMs. However, their coarse-grained estimation inevitably leads to performance degradation at high sparsity rates.

arxiv-2511-10723.title: Reaching for the Edge II: Stellar Halos out to Large Radii as a Tracer of Dark Matter Halo Mass 2025 Reaching for the Edge II: Stellar Halos out to Large Radii as a Tracer of Dark Matter Halo Mass – References
arxiv-2511-10723.creator: Katya Leidig, Benedikt Diemer, Song Huang (黄崧), Shuo Xu (许朔), Conghao Zhou (周丛浩), Alexie Leauthaud
arxiv-2511-10723.description: Abstract The diffuse outskirts of brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) encode valuable information about the assembly history and mass of their host dark matter halos. However, the low surface brightness of these stellar halos has historically made them difficult to observe.

arxiv-2512-13358.title: Diffusiophoretic migration of colloidal particles in sucrose gradients
arxiv-2512-13358.creator: Antoine Monier, Brielle Byerley, Julien Renaudeau, H. Daniel Ou-Yang, Pierre Lidon, Jean-Baptiste Salmon
arxiv-2512-13358.description: Abstract Diffusiophoresis (DP) refers to the migration of particles driven by a solute concentration gradient in a liquid. Observations in the case of molecular neutral solutes are rather scarce, due to the low drift velocities in dilute solutions, and the difficulty in distinguishing DP from other phenomena in concentrated solutions.

Previous genetic studies have identified common risk variants which have progressively increased in number with increasing sample sizes of the respective studies. Here, we conduct a genome-wide...

europmc-pmc6468149.creator: Boopathy GTK, Hong W.
europmc-pmc6468149.description: Angiogenesis is a highly coordinated process of formation of new blood vessels from pre-existing blood vessels. The process of development of the proper vascular network is a complex process that is crucial for the vertebrate development. Several studies have defined essential...

pmc-10621164.title: A practical guide to in situ and ex situ characterisation of arabinogalactan proteins (AGPs) in fruits
pmc-10621164.creator: Nataliia Kutyrieva-Nowak, Agata Leszczuk, Artur Zdunek
pmc-10621164.description: BackgroundArabinogalactan proteins (AGPs) are plant cell components found in the extracellular matrix that play crucial roles in fruit growth and development. AGPs demonstrate structural diversity due to the presence of a protein domain and an expanded carbohydrate moiety. Considering their molecular structure, the modification of glycosylation is a primary factor contributing to the functional variety of AGPs.

pmc-10672591.title: Influence of Long-Term Storage and UV Light Exposure on Characteristics of Polyurethane Foams for Cryogenic Insulation
pmc-10672591.creator: Beatrise Sture, Vladimir Yakushin, Laima Vevere, Ugis Cabulis
pmc-10672591.description: Rigid polyurethane (PUR) foams have been the most effective insulation material used in space launchers since the beginning of cryogenic fuel use, due to their outstanding thermal and mechanical properties. In this study, spray-applied PUR foams using different ratios of amine-based catalysts were produced.

pmc-11424641.title: 11-month-olds recognize the teacher–student relationship
pmc-11424641.creator: Ruolan Ling, Reiko Matsunaka, Kazuo Hiraki
pmc-11424641.description: Understanding how preverbal infants perceive and differentiate the roles of teachers and students can provide profound insights into the early stages of human learning and cognition. We thus developed a paradigm based on the task order and the interactive position to determine if infants understand teacher–student relationships.

pmc-11436981.title: Case study of the environmental impacts and benefits of a PBF-LB additively manufactured optimized filtrate nozzle
pmc-11436981.creator: Pasi Puukko, Lotta Hepo-oja, Saija Vatanen, Janne Kaipainen, Marja-Leena Mäkinen, Markku Lindqvist
pmc-11436981.description: In this paper, we present a comprehensive case study of a laser-based powder bed fusion-manufactured optimized filtrate nozzle, focusing on environmental impacts and benefits. The scope of the study covers the raw material production, part manufacturing and use phases. We compare the results for similar components manufactured by conventional, mainly material-removing manufacturing technologies.

pmc-11447563.title: Addressing unique challenges and crafting inclusive policies for Queer living with disabilities
pmc-11447563.creator: Ikekhwa A. Ikhile, Azwihangwisi H. Mavhandu-Mudzusi, Ndlovu Sinegugu
pmc-11447563.description: BackgroundThis article addresses the intersectional challenges faced by Queer people living with disabilities (QPwD).ObjectivesThe article aims to highlight the nature and extent of their struggles while proposing inclusive policies for societal integration and equality. Amid global efforts to promote Queer rights, discrimination and violence persist, particularly affecting those with disabilities.

pmc-11484760.title: India’s evolving digital health strategy
pmc-11484760.creator: Aditya Narayan, Indu Bhushan, Kevin Schulman
pmc-11484760.description: India’s evolving digital health strategy leverages innovative technologies to enhance access to healthcare services. This paper explores the key components of India’s digital health transformation, including the Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABDM) and India’s integration of biometric identification and digital infrastructure to improve healthcare delivery.

pmc-11580190.title: HIV phylogenetic clusters point to unmet hiv prevention, testing and treatment needs among men who have sex with men in kenya
pmc-11580190.creator: François Cholette, Lisa Lazarus, Pascal Macharia, Jeffrey Walimbwa, Samuel Kuria, Parinita Bhattacharjee, Helgar Musyoki, Mary Mugambi, Martin K Ongaro, Kennedy Olango, Janet Musimbi, Faran Emmanuel, Shajy Isac, Michael Pickles, Marissa L Becker, Sharmistha Mishra, Lyle R McKinnon, James Blanchard,
pmc-11580190.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundThe HIV epidemic in Kenya remains a significant public health concern, particularly among gay, bisexual, and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM), who continue to bear a disproportionate burden of the epidemic.

pmc-11607770.title: Early-stage hypertension defined by the 2017 ACC/AHA blood pressure guideline carries excessive cardiovascular risk in axial spondyloarthritis patients
pmc-11607770.creator: Lin-Hong Shi, Ho So, Steven Ho Man Lam, Tena K Li, Edmund Li, Cheuk-Chun Szeto, Lai-Shan Tam
pmc-11607770.description: Background:Hypertension (HTN) is the most important modifiable risk factor for the development of cardiovascular events (CVEs). Patients with axSpA are also associated with an increased risk of future CVE.Objectives:To ascertain whether baseline early-stage HTN is a predictor of future CVE in addition to inflammation in patients with axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA).Design:A retrospective cohort study.

pmc-12504706.title: Photocatalytic degradation of amoxicillin in aqueous solutions using rGO/BiFeO3 nanocomposites in the presence of LED light irradiation
pmc-12504706.creator: Leila Mersa, Abdolmotaleb Seid-mohammadi, Mohammad Reza Samarghandi, Mohammad Khazaei, Ghorban Asgari
pmc-12504706.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In current study, a simple hydrothermal approach was used to synthesis of BiFeO3 nanocomposites on reduced graphene oxide (rGO/BiFeO3) under visible LED light (Vis LED) for photocatalytic degradation of amoxicillin. X-ray diffraction (XRD), field emission scanning electron microscope (FE-SEM), and energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) techniques were applied for characterization of the structural, optical, and surface morphological properties of the synthesized catalysts.

pmc-12592428.title: Mapping the phenomenology of intranasal 5-MeO-DMT in psychedelic-naïve healthy adults
pmc-12592428.creator: Anna O Ermakova, Fiona Dunbar, Mathieu Seynaeve, Raphaël Millière
pmc-12592428.description: 5-Methoxy-N,N-dimethyltryptamine (5-MeO-DMT) is a naturally occurring psychedelic tryptamine. Plants containing 5-MeO-DMT have been used throughout history, and in recent years both synthetic and toad-derived 5-MeO-DMT use is being increasingly reported in naturalistic settings as well as clinical research. However, its subjective effects are not well characterised, and no qualitative research studies have been published to date.

pmc-12630252.title: Influence of the number of images on threshold image contrast measurements with a phantom with gold disks in digital mammography
pmc-12630252.creator: Michał Biegała, Agata Batolik
pmc-12630252.description: Image quality, in addition to radiation dose, is the most important physical parameter in digital mammography. Image quality should be periodically monitored using the CDMAM phantom. The aim of this study is to investigate the effect of the number of analyzed images on the result of threshold image contrast measurements using the CDMAM phantom in different versions.

pmc-12660811.title: Action repetition biases choice in context-dependent decision-making
pmc-12660811.creator: Ben J Wagner, H Benedikt Wolf, Stefan J Kiebel
pmc-12660811.description: Humans are prone to decision biases, which make behavior seemingly irrational. An important cause for decision biases is that the context in which decisions are made can later influence which choices humans prefer in new situations. Current computational models (e.g. relative value learning or range normalization) often require extensive environmental knowledge to explain these biases.

pmc-13108233.title: The Relevance of Crystal Clear and Unclear Days to Evaluate Residual Interictal Burden in Patients With Migraine Treated With CGRP Monoclonal Antibodies
pmc-13108233.creator: Marcello Silvestro, Ilaria Orologio, Raffaele Ornello, Francesca Trojsi, Alessandro Tessitore, Simona Sacco, Antonio Russo
pmc-13108233.description: BackgroundAlthough treatment goals in migraine prevention have moved beyond the benchmark of a 50% reduction in monthly attacks, residual disease burden is still evaluated based on residual headache frequency. However, migraine‐related symptoms can persist despite headache freedom, leading to so‐called unclear days that may meaningfully contribute to interictal burden.
